description: The external comparison register required by .kiro/specs/multi-raft-performance/ Requirement 9. One record per external number. Every field of Appendix A is present on every record; a field the source does not state carries the literal string 'not stated' and is NEVER inferred (9.2). A number that cannot be sourced to a retrievable document is not entered at all (9.3), and a record may exist purely to say why.

records.implementation_version: etcd 3.2.0 (published on the v3.5 documentation site; the benchmark itself was run against 3.2.0 with Go 1.8.3)
records.hardware: Google Cloud Compute Engine. 3 etcd servers, each 8 vCPU, 16 GB memory, 50 GB SSD. 1 client machine, 16 vCPU, 30 GB memory, 50 GB SSD. Ubuntu 17.04. CPU model not stated; network performance not stated; SSD class and IOPS not stated.
records.cluster_size_replication_factor: 3 members; replication factor 3 (every etcd member holds the full log)
records.durability: not stated on the page (etcd fsyncs its WAL by default, but the page does not say so and 9.2 forbids inferring it)
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: 10,000 keys, target Leader: 583 QPS, average latency 1.6 ms, 48 MB memory
records.comparison_class: indicative — external system is a database with its own WAL and boltdb storage engine (9.5); our tiers below C cannot carry a like-for-like claim at all (3.3)

records.implementation_version: Dragonboat v3 (the README describes v3 as the latest release; the hardware document is docs/test.md on master)
records.hardware: "Three servers each with a single 22-core Intel XEON E5-2696v4 processor, all cores can boost to 2.8Ghz", "40GE Mellanox NIC", "Intel 900P for storing the RocksDB's WAL and Intel P3700 1.6T for storing all other data", "Ubuntu 16.04 with Spectre and Meltdown patches, ext4 file-system". Memory not stated.
records.cluster_size_replication_factor: 3 servers; replication factor not stated (three NodeHost instances across three servers implies 3, but the source does not say it)
records.raft_group_count: "48 Raft shards on three NodeHost instances across three servers"
records.payload_size: 16 bytes value; key size not stated (16, 128 and 1024 byte payloads were all tested)
records.read_write_mix: 100% write for the 9 million figure; 9:1 read:write for the 11 million figure
records.client_concurrency: not stated as a count — "Each request is handled in its own goroutine"
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: "9 million writes per second when the payload is 16bytes each or 11 million mixed I/O per second at 9:1 read:write ratio"
records.comparison_class: indicative — the closest peer in kind (a multi-group Raft library), but every axis except payload size is mismatched: 22 cores per node against our 8, NVMe-backed fsync against our memory persistence, 48 groups against our 4, and a client concurrency the source does not state

records.hardware: As above. The README additionally states CPU usage of "3 cores (2.8GHz) on each server" for this figure.
records.payload_size: 16 bytes value; key size not stated
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: "1.25 million per second when payload is 16 bytes each, average latency is 1.3ms and the P99 latency is 2.6ms"
records.comparison_class: indicative — single-group library figure, which is the closest in shape to our Zipfian hot-group arm, but fsync-durable against our memory persistence and on 22-core hardware

records.hardware: As above; the README's latency table does not restate it.
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: "<5ms P99 write latency when handling 8 million writes per second at 16 bytes each"
records.comparison_class: indicative — this is the only external p99 write figure in the register, and it is stated as a bound ("<5ms") rather than a value

records.hardware: As above, with "30ms" RTT between nodes; the README does not say how the RTT was produced (real distance or injected).
records.read_write_mix: "I/O" — mix not stated for this figure
records.client_concurrency: "a much larger number of clients" — count not stated
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: "2 million I/O per second can still be achieved using a much larger number of clients" at 30 ms RTT
records.comparison_class: indicative, and thin — payload size, mix and client count are all unstated, so this record exists mainly to bound what a WAN figure looks like for a library of this kind

records.implementation_version: braft, master branch (no version is stated on the benchmark document)
records.hardware: 12 cores, Intel Xeon E5-2620 v2 @ 2.10GHz; LENOVO SAS 300G (approximately 800 IOPS random write, approximately 200 MB/s sequential write); 10 Gigabit NIC with multi-queue not enabled. Memory not stated.
records.payload_size: 512 bytes among others; the full set of sizes is only legible from the charts
records.read_write_mix: 100% write (synchronous RPC writes committed through the Raft group)
records.durability: sync enabled (the document states sync is on by default for all of these tests)
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: NO NUMBER IS ENTERED. braft publishes its QPS and latency results only as images (benchmark0.png, benchmark.png); the document's text carries the configuration but no figure. Requirement 9.3 forbids using a number that cannot be sourced to a retrievable document, and a chart read by eye is not one.
records.comparison_class: no comparison — the C++ multi-group peer Requirement 9.4 asks for is present in the register as a configuration record and as a stated absence, not as a number

records.hardware: Virtual machines. Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2630 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 40 vCPU, 64 GiB memory, 500 GiB NVMe SSD. Network not stated.
records.cluster_size_replication_factor: 3 TiKV nodes; replication factor not stated. PD node count and client node count not stated on this page.
records.raft_group_count: not stated — TiKV shards into Regions and the page does not say how many the 10M-record dataset produced
records.payload_size: not stated (go-ycsb defaults are not restated on the page)
records.read_write_mix: workload C (100% read) for the point-get figure
records.client_concurrency: not stated in the text — the page varies it across figures without listing the values
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: "212,000 OPS" point-get read, workload C, 10M records and 10M operations, measured with GO YCSB; "average latency less than 10 milliseconds"
records.comparison_class: indicative — TiKV is a database: the number includes RocksDB and, on the transactional path, a transaction layer (9.5). This is also the implementation this project's multi-raft design is explicitly drawn from, which makes it the most interesting record and not the most comparable one.

records.hardware: Virtual machines. Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2630 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 40 vCPU, 64 GiB memory, 500 GiB NVMe SSD. Network not stated.
records.cluster_size_replication_factor: 3 TiKV nodes; replication factor not stated
records.read_write_mix: workload A (50% read, 50% update) for the update figure
records.metric_and_unit_as_stated: "43,200 OPS" update, workload A, 10M records and 10M operations, measured with GO YCSB. The p99 latency is published as a figure only and is not entered.
records.comparison_class: indicative — database with a storage engine (9.5); payload size and client concurrency both unstated, which are the two axes a write comparison most needs
